subject: Re: Model fit & evals follow-up — function-calling / structured output
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finpay.com>, Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T15:12:00Z
Subject: Model fit & evals follow-up — function-calling / structured output

Thanks again for the productive call today — great to meet the FinPay team. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: reliably extract structured payment details from merchant emails and webhook payloads (amount, currency, timestamp, merchant_id, status, failure_reason) with JSON-schema validation and deterministic function outputs.
- Success criteria you shared: schema_match_rate >= 99% on production prompt set; mean token latency < 300ms for 16-token outputs; <0.1% false-positive chargebacks.

Redwood recommendations (initial)
- Models to evaluate: redwood-llama-70b-q4 (best quality/cost tradeoff) and redwood-mistral-22b (lower-latency A/B baseline).
- Eval types: 1) functional schema compliance (JSON output + strict schema validation), 2) robustness to noisy inputs (OCR artifacts, truncated threads), 3) retries/backoff behaviour for transient failures.

Deliverables we propose
- 48–72 hour eval run against your supplied prompt set + edge-case augmentations.
- Benchmarks we will produce: schema_match_rate, per-field precision/recall, avg retries per request, median and p95 token latency, per-model cost estimate.
- Suggested guardrails: automatic fallback to smaller FP model for low-latency routes; prefix caching for frequent merchants.

Attachments and links
- Attached: finpay-prompt-set-v1.csv (your prompts), payment_schema.json (please confirm this is the canonical schema).
- Public benchmark template we'll use: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finpay-evals

Next steps / asks
1) Can you confirm payment_schema.json is the authoritative schema and flag any additional fields to include?
2) Confirm a 72-hour eval window starting Mon 2026-11-09 — ok with your team?
3) To Neha (cc): can you scope an eval harness that includes function-calling tests with retries/backoff sim?
4) To Rishi: please prepare a short security note on data retention and KMS handling for evaluation artifacts.

We’ll share a live dashboard (read-only) with per-model metrics and a short executive summary at the end of the run.

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast on this.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: finpay-prompt-set-v1.csv; redwood-benchmarks-nov2026.pdf; payment_schema.json

From: Elena Rossi <elena@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Model fit & evals follow-up — function-calling / structured output

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) payment_schema.json — attached (we also included a few additional optional fields: merchant_notes, refund_policy_code). Please incorporate if possible.
2) Retries/backoff behaviour: for idempotent webhook parsing we want 2 retries with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms) and a max total time of 2s before marking as transient-failure. Can your eval harness simulate downstream timeouts?
3) Edge cases: we'll add 120 synthetic samples with OCR noise and 50 samples with nested quotes. Please include these in the run.
4) Cost: can you provide a rough token estimate for the 72-hour run (we're particularly sensitive to Q4 billing).

Also looping in our engineering lead Mike for any infra questions. We're good to start Monday — please proceed once Rishi/Neha confirm ops.

—
Elena Rossi
Head of Integrations, FinPay
elena@finpay.com

FYI — forwarding FinPay's clarifications. TL;DR: they want schema validation + explicit retry/backoff behaviour in the harness, plus the 120 OCR/noise samples.

Rishi / Neha — can you own the following?
- Neha: build the eval harness and schedule the 72-hour run. Include: function-calling tests that validate JSON outputs against payment_schema.json (attached), noisy input augmentation, and a small A/B between redwood-llama-70b-q4 and redwood-mistral-22b. Provide a cost estimate (tokens + infra) before we start.
- Rishi: prepare a short security note (KMS usage for encryption at rest, retention policy for eval artifacts, SOC2 scope implications). Also confirm that eval logs will be scrubbed of PII before being persisted.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Use automatic prefix caching and batching where appropriate; we should measure impact on latency and unit cost.
- For function-calling, validate strict JSON schema compliance; mark a request as failure if parser output doesn't adhere to schema. For transient parse errors, implement 2 retries with exponential backoff (200ms, 600ms).
- If schema_match_rate < 98% for a model on the first run, flag for manual prompt engineering and schedule a follow-up quick-turn prompt tuning iteration.

Let me know if you need additional context from FinPay.

—
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Model fit & evals follow-up — function-calling / structured output

Thanks Marissa — will take point. High-level plan and commitments below: 

Plan
1) Eval harness: Neha will spin up the harness today. It will:
   - Run parallel A/B on redwood-llama-70b-q4 and redwood-mistral-22b for 72 hours.
   - Include 120 OCR/noise samples and 50 nested-quote samples from FinPay.
   - Validate outputs against payment_schema.json (strict mode).
   - Implement retry policy: 2 retries with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms). Retries will be counted and surfaced in the dashboard.

2) Metrics & thresholds:
   - schema_match_rate (target >= 99% for go/no-go)
   - per-field precision/recall (report per-field failure modes)
   - avg retries per request (target < 0.05)
   - median/p95 token latency and cost per 1k requests

3) Security & data handling (Rishi)
   - Eval artifacts will be encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys and retained for 30 days by default.
   - Logs will be scrubbed for PII; any raw merchant IDs will be hashed before storage.
   - We'll produce a short evidence pack for FinPay with retention and KMS configuration.

Timeline & cost
- Setup + dry-run: 12 hours.
- Full run: 72 hours.
- Executive summary and dashboard: within 24 hours after run completes.
- Preliminary cost estimate: ~USD 1,400–2,000 for the 72-hour A/B run (model mix dependent). Neha will provide a token-level estimate before starting.

Next actions
- Neha: share the harness link and token-cost estimate by EOD.
- Elena / Mike: confirm we can proceed with the 72-hour start window tomorrow morning.

Elena — tagging you to confirm the schema changes (merchant_notes, refund_policy_code) are acceptable; if yes we'll include them in strict validation.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Applied ML — Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
